newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian journalists freed in Chechnya-TV station.
newsitem.headline: Russian journalists freed in Chechnya-TV station.

text.p: Three Russian journalists taken hostage by unknown gunmen in Chechnya more than three months ago have been freed, NTV television said on Monday.

The news, reported by the commercial channel, came as Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen rebel leader Aslan Maskhadov held talks in Moscow. The presenter said the three were now on their way to the capital.
The capture of the three, including award-winning correspondent Yelena Masyuk, became a sticking-point in relations between Russia and its breakaway Chechen republic.
Moscow accused the Chechens of being unable to control the situation in the region, torn by 21 months of war between separatists and Russian troops which ended a year ago.
The Chechens said the Russians were encouraging a wave of hostage-takings in and around Chechnya. Two Britons, a German, a Slovak and four French aid workers are still being held.

Monday's talks in Moscow are aimed at breaking the deadlock over whether Chechnya should be independent or remain part of the Russian Federation. The stalemate has held up post-war reconstruction and complicated a lucrative oil transport deal.
